### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `193e37893e16b76a7be85a38fd5f69e814707130` — the merge of head `3d92094558cb3739ac60893c332786494aa88767` into base `c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 193e37893e16b76a7be85a38fd5f69e814707130 && git checkout 193e37893e16b76a7be85a38fd5f69e814707130
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 3d92094558cb3739ac60893c332786494aa88767 && git checkout -B drift-repro c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 && git merge --no-ff 3d92094558cb3739ac60893c332786494aa88767

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Head-sha: 233683d6ee98accf75b8a0dd6e0ae6324c861e68
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34870 (the D3 rule 1 qualifier that maintainer ruling 6946563869 on #34720 asks for; os-dev report 6954260196).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Closes #34870`. No other issue sits next to a closing verb. Two paths, +23/-3.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34928`: GOVERNED, landing tier H, on 1 of 2 paths (`docs/adr/**`). The low-risk skills arm does not apply, since this is an ADR rule text. The route is the seat's fable L2 (a rules face), then the seat's Tier H record and os-zhuang's hand. The area never readies it.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`. There is no changeset: `dataset-term-matcher.ts` changes by doc comments only, and `Check Changeset` is green.

**Check-runs at 233683d6, read at about 16:36Z.** 56 runs, none failed. Already `success`: `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Test UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. Still `in_progress`: `Build Core`, all 10 Test Core shards, `Live E2E UI`, the remaining Lint legs and the four `Type Check ·` legs. This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**Against the ruling.** I read 6946563869 on #34720. The option text quoted, 「A+C 本语言标签+同义词」, is byte-identical. The note carries each part of the ruling's execution:
- A: a bundle label is matched only in the caller's locale, resolved before matching.
- C: a cross-locale word is an authored `synonym`, and `candidates` does not rescue it.
- The D3 wording: every locale of an inline map, plus the bundle label in the caller's locale, and the matcher's doc comment says the same.
- The known consequence: under a translated locale, an English source label that is not the member's `name` misses.

**Add-only.** The ADR diff is 10 `+` lines and 0 `-` lines. The note is nested under rule 1 in ADR-0011's `> **Amendment note**` form, the same form #34828 used after rule 5. It says it changes no other word of rule 1, and rule 1's text is untouched.

**Each code claim, checked on this head.** Every symbol anchor resolves:
- **The bundle answer replaces the authored label, inline map included.** In `i18n-resolver.ts` `translateDatasetMembers`, when `lookupDatasetMemberAttr` answers, the member is returned with `label` set to that string, whatever was authored. When it does not answer, `raw` is kept, inline map and all. So the note's 「it takes the place of the authored label … so the authored label is then no target」 is exact, and it correctly does not suggest both are targets.
- **HTTP.** `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts#datasetToolMembers` runs `translateMetaList` with `requestLocale` set to `metaRequestLocale({ headers: context.request?.headers }, i18n)`. That reads `Accept-Language`, then `?locale=`, then the i18n service's `getDefaultLocale()`.
- **stdio.** `stdio-data-bridge.ts` (around line 1453 on this head) runs the same `translateMetaList` with `metaRequestLocale(undefined, i18n)`, which means the i18n default locale. The dev's corrected premise holds: the stdio translation from #34833 is on `main`.
- **No i18n service.** In both doors, the resolver failure is caught and the untranslated list is returned, so the authored label alone is the target. That matches the note.
- **The matcher.** It never reads the bundle. Its two doc-comment edits say the same as the note in the same words, and no code changes.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. 「resolved for the caller's locale」 includes the resolver's locale chain. `localeChain` consults the requested locale, then the declared `fallbackChain` (skipped when the requested locale is the authored default). So a caller in `zh-TW` with a `zh-CN` fallback is served, and matched on, the `zh-CN` bundle value when `zh-TW` has none. The note's 「only that resolved value is a target」 already covers this, because it is still one served value. If L2 wants it spelled out, add 「(along the locale's fallback chain)」 after 「the caller's locale」. Not owed.
- N2. The ruling said the note "can ride #34761's ADR-0149 note". It rides its own card instead, because #34828 had already landed its note. That is fine: the two notes sit under rule 1 and after rule 5, and they cross-reference each other (C's bullet points to the `candidates` note).
- N3. #34904 changes the same matcher file (code, not comments). `overlap-check` is clean against it, as the body reports. Whichever lands second should re-run the service-analytics typecheck.

Next: the seat's fable L2 (rules face), then the seat's Tier H record and os-zhuang. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `233683d6ee98accf75b8a0dd6e0ae6324c861e68`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0149-ai-answers-business-questions-through-the-dataset-semantic-layer.md + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-term-matcher.ts
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #34870 (body and its three comments: triage 6951462561, claim 6953575714, os-dev report 6954260196); PR #34928 body, file list (2 paths, +23/-3) and the net diff against `main` (merge base `ab441988`; `main` at `189358f2` moves none of the files this review reads); the 59 check-runs on this head. The ruling record 6946563869 on #34720 was read because the diff quotes it. Code outside the diff was read on this head, never reviewed.

Check-runs on `233683d6`, read 2026-11-17T16:57Z: 59 runs, all completed: 38 `success`, 21 `skipped`, none failed, cancelled or timed out. Green among them: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Documentation Links`, every `Lint ·` leg, the four `Type Check ·` legs, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: none changes. The diff holds no statement, type, export or schema edit; the matcher's code lines are byte-unchanged. Right.
- Public surface: `MatchableMember.label` and the module comment gain doc text only. `MatchableMember` is exported, so the published declaration file carries a longer comment and nothing else. Right.
- Rule text: ADR-0149 D3 rule 1 is untouched (10 added lines, 0 removed); the note qualifies the label target and says it changes no other word. Right.
- The matcher's behaviour as the note states it, read in `matchDatasetTerms` / `labelTargets`: a string label is one target, a plain-object label contributes each string value, the bundle is never read. Right.
- The note's account of WHICH bundle value the matcher is handed is wrong in one clause: S1 below.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. Agreed. No changeset, label `skip-changeset`, `Check Changeset` green. The ADR is not published; the package diff is comments only, so nothing ships that a consumer can observe. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag 1, the dispatch's stdio premise was stale: confirmed. `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts#createStdioDataBridge` runs `translateMetaList` with `metaRequestLocale(undefined, i18n)`, the i18n service's default locale. The note states the code, which is right.
- Dev flag 2, attribution line and plain-text trailer: PR-body form, `PR-body guards` is green; not a contract matter.
- Dev flag 3 (PR body), the bundle replaces and does not add: confirmed in `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`, `translateDatasetMembers`: when the member lookup answers, `label` is set to that string whatever was authored; when it does not, the raw member is returned, inline map included.
- Overlap with open PR #34904 on the same file: the lane seat's; no contract effect here.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation, no join in the diff.
- Security: no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The matcher's "admitted members only" sentence is pre-existing and untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. One should-fix, owing a delta review. Three nits.

**S1 (should-fix) — "the caller's locale only … the bundle's values in other locales are not" is contradicted by the resolver the note cites.**
The bundle label is not read at the caller's locale alone. `lookupDatasetMemberAttr` walks `localeChain(opts)`, and `metaTranslateOptions` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`) fills that chain with the deployment's declared fallback locale (`getFallbackLocale()`), skipped only when the caller's locale is the authored one. Each step is then read through `pickData` / `resolveBundleLocale`, the platform locale ladder (case, table language, base language, variant expansion). So on this head:
  - a `zh-TW` caller against a bundle that holds `zh-CN` and no Traditional key is served, and matched on, the `zh-CN` value, with no fallback declared at all (variant expansion);
  - a `fr` caller in a deployment with fallback `en` is served, and matched on, the `en` bundle value, and by the note's own replacement rule the authored label is then NO target.
A reader of the note predicts the opposite in both cases: no bundle value for my locale, so the bundle does not answer, so the authored label still matches. That reader is the one the note is written for: the app author deciding which words must be authored as `synonym` entries (option C, the remedy the note prescribes), and the D5 scenario author writing expected hits and misses. Both get it wrong for any deployment with a declared fallback or a regional variant. The half-sentence "only that resolved value is a target" is true; the next clause and the bold lead deny what "resolved" includes. The ruling itself anchors option A to "today's HTTP behaviour", so spelling the chain out restates the ruling, it does not widen it.
Fix, prose only, in the note's bundle point and mirrored in one clause of the matcher's module comment: say the bundle label is resolved for the caller's locale along the resolver's locale chain (the requested locale by the platform locale ladder, then the deployment's declared fallback locale, which is skipped when the caller's locale is the authored one); exactly one value is served per member and only that value is a target; and replace "the bundle's values in other locales are not" with "no other bundle value is". The symbol to anchor is `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts#metaTranslateOptions`.

- N1 (nit) — "a host whose i18n service cannot be resolved serves the catalogue untranslated" is exact on stdio (no service, no locale, `translateMetaList` returns the items) and has one corner on HTTP: with an `Accept-Language` header a locale still resolves, and a dataset that is a `.custom` pair's declared override is still handed its pair's own translations (`pairTranslationBundleOf`, read from the protocol, not from the i18n service), which `labelCatalogs` then applies. Rare enough (authored pair translations on a host with no i18n service) to leave or to soften with "apart from a declared override's pair translations". No effect on the ruled rule.
- N2 (nit) — "per transport" lists the HTTP door and stdio. D2 names a third caller of the same executor, cloud's service-ai registry, which supplies its own `loadDatasets`. The matcher comment's "the transport localizes the catalogue before it runs" covers it in the code; the note could say in half a sentence that any other door owes the same translation step. Accepted deviation or a follow-up card.
- N3 (nit) — the note header says "this PR" with no number. It follows the #34761 note in the same record, so it is consistent here, but ADR-0011's note names the PR and commit. Leave it, or fold into a status-hygiene pass.

Judged and found to hold:
- Ruling quote: 「A+C 本语言标签+同义词」 is byte-identical in the ADR note, in the matcher comment and in ruling record 6946563869 (compared as bytes). The record id and its link are right, and the note's four parts (A, C, the D3 wording, the known consequence) are each the ruling's.
- Inline map point: every locale is a target unless the bundle answers. Holds (`labelTargets`, and the pass-through of the raw member when the lookup misses).
- Option C point: synonyms are never translated (`translateDataset` docblock, D1's i18n stance); `candidates` offer and never hit, as the rule 5 note says. The D1 fragment link matches the heading.
- HTTP: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts#datasetToolMembers` hands `metaRequestLocale` the request headers only, so `Accept-Language`, else the i18n default. Holds; the `?locale=` arm is unreachable there and the note rightly omits it.
- stdio: holds, as in ③.
- "The matcher is unchanged" and "its doc comment says the same": hold. The two comment edits say the note's words; `MatchableMember.label`'s "arrives already resolved … as a string" is what `translateDatasetMembers` writes.
- Carrier: an add-only `Amendment note` blockquote nested under the rule it qualifies is the record's own form (the #34761 note after rule 5) and the registry's (40 such notes across `docs/adr/`; AGENTS.md names "add-only ADR notes" as a landing class). The note narrows how a sentence is read and reverses no decision, so no new ADR and no status-line change is owed. Right carrier.
- All six symbol anchors in the note resolve on this head (`Lint · docs & code guards` is green; each was also read).

Verdict on this head: PASS, with S1 open. S1 is a prose-face fix that moves the head; the delta review of that fix is owed before this record can clear.

Head-sha: 4b963c9824ac155296328f5a8723915650155995
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c. This is a delta read of `233683d6`..`4b963c98` against my 6954336709, answering the seat's fable L2 S1 (6954921504) and my N1 (os-dev report 6956227841).

### 席位核对

**Delta.** Prose only, on the same two paths:
- the ADR-0149 D3 rule 1 note;
- the matcher's module comment and the `label` doc. The code lines are byte-unchanged.

The note is still add-only against `main`: every changed line sits inside the PR's own note. The tier is still H (`docs/adr/**`). CI at report time: none failed, some legs still running. This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**L2 S1 and my N1: closed.** The bundle point now names the chain, and I checked each symbol on this head:
- `i18n-resolver.ts#lookupDatasetMemberAttr` (:2521) reads along `localeChain`.
- `i18n-resolver.ts#resolveBundleLocale` (:543) documents the ladder "exact → case-insensitive → platform table language → base-language → variant-expansion". That is the note's 「case, platform table language, base language, variant expansion」.
- `meta-item-read-gate.ts#metaTranslateOptions` (:3286) sets `fallbackChain` from `getFallbackLocale()` and `defaultLocale` from the source or default locale. `localeChain` skips the fallback when the requested locale is that default. That matches the note's 「skipped when the caller's locale is the one the labels are authored in」.
- Both worked cases follow from that: `zh-TW` reaches a `zh-CN`-only bundle by variant expansion with no fallback declared, and `fr` reaches the `en` label through a declared `en` fallback.
- 「One value is served per member … no other bundle value is」 states the invariant exactly. The bold lead and the matcher comment say the same in one clause each.

**L2 nits folded.**
- **N1, the HTTP pair exception.** In `translateMetaList`, the locale comes from `requestLocale(i18n)`, which on HTTP still answers from `Accept-Language` when the i18n service is absent. `pairTranslationBundleOf` (:3398) is read from the protocol, so a `.custom` pair's override can still be translated with no i18n service. On stdio, `metaRequestLocale(undefined, undefined)` is `undefined`, and the list returns untranslated. So 「the one exception is on HTTP」 is exact.
- **N2, other doors.** `dataset-tools.ts#DatasetToolsDeps` (:156) is where an external door supplies `loadDatasets`, and the note puts the translation duty there, with cloud's `ToolRegistry` as the example.
- **N3.** The header reads 「PR #34928」.

**Anchors.** `adr-symbol-anchors` passes with the five new anchors, as the report says. Every one resolves to the line I read.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. The branch is 11 behind `main`. Nothing in that gap touches the ADR or the matcher's doc comment, as far as `overlap-check` (clean, #34904 included) shows. A merge of `main` before the Tier H record is the seat's call.

Next: the seat's L2 delta, then the Tier H record and os-zhuang. #34943 folds the same wording, and its delta read follows. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

Everything the earlier record judged and this delta does not touch stands as written there.

The two failures are one event: `Type Check · workspace` (job 134234042188) ended on "The action 'Checkout repository' has timed out after 20 minutes", so no type check ran, and the aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` reports that leg. ### ① Derived judgments

- Still prose and comments only. Against the merge base the package file changes comment lines alone (every changed line sits inside a doc block; no statement, type or export moves); the ADR is 10 added lines, 0 removed, all inside the PR's own note. Right.
- Accept-set and public surface: unchanged from the earlier record. The exported `MatchableMember.label` carries a reworded comment. Right.

  - `resolveBundleLocale` is the ladder each step is read through; the note's "case, platform table language, base language, variant expansion" is its documented order after the exact match.

No must-fix. No should-fix. Two new nits.

The three earlier nits, folded in this delta, were re-read for new error and none was found:

- The five new symbol anchors (`lookupDatasetMemberAttr`, `resolveBundleLocale`, `metaTranslateOptions`, `pairTranslationBundleOf`, `DatasetToolsDeps`) each resolve to a declaration on this head, and `Lint · docs & code guards` is green.

New nits, neither affecting correctness or the contract:
- N4 (nit) — the declared fallback locale is itself read through the same ladder; the note describes the ladder for the requested locale only. Not false, one step short of complete.
- N5 (nit) — the PR title still reads "in the caller's locale only", the wording this delta retired from the tree. A title edit moves no head.

Verdict on this head: the contract holds, S1 is closed and nothing graded is open. The red `Type Check · workspace` is an unmeasured gate, not a finding against the diff; it must be re-run to green on this head before the record is used to land anything.
